title: Instructor surfaces and screen-reader labels use plain words and the D17 effort words
acceptance: The meta and Open Graph descriptions match the canon: movement-first, Cycle, Pilates and HIIT, not "spin".
The landing page names the disciplines and the job in the first screen; the §12.4 subhead and "See class shape" label are used or the deviation is recorded.
Class Pulse accessible labels use Build, Push, Attack and All Out, and summarize the class (duration, peaks) instead of listing every track.

The jargon listed in the audit (docs/audits/ux-audit-2026-10-28/README.md, cross-cutting theme 3 and the Principle 0 Q3 rows) is replaced with plain words, not helper text: "provider truth", "pressure-safe view", "creative loop", "provider-authorized playback", "movement language", "separate capabilities", "Public widget ready", "your authorized library", "carry the source into class work", "clip decisions", "SOURCE → DESTINATION", "MUSIC SOURCES", "PERSONAL WORKSPACE", and "Catalog" used where instructors read "Songs".
Sign-in copy: "Invited? Create your account.", a clear invitation-email line, and one "Private beta" mention.
nextAction: One copy PR. Files: apps/web/index.html, MarketingPage.tsx, Login.tsx, ClassPulse.tsx, CreateClassDialog.tsx, Dashboard.tsx, providers.ts. Judgment items (core pain line, hero demo class) are proposed in the PR for the owner. providers.ts is owner-gated (scripts/owner-gate.mjs), so the PR needs owner-approved if it touches it. Surface: web.
